recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-36814 unless PA makes a new decision to reopen the Appointment.start/end datatype question.
issue_request: Published PA issue, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking whether Appointment.start/end were too constrained as instant. The final disposition kept start/end as instant, directed not-yet-solidified times to requestedPeriod, moved requestedPeriod after start/end/length, and added comments to Appointment.start and Appointment.end.
initial_application: Git commit 1bd6618a0590a3b5f79d79f9a143c1f77235d91d explicitly applied FHIR-36814 by adding the requested comment to Appointment.start and Appointment.end and moving Appointment.requestedPeriod next to the time-related elements. No datatype widening was applied, matching the Jira disposition.
additional_context: Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini. PA's 2022-09-07 minutes record the same 4-0-0 not-persuasive-with-modification motion. Earlier FHIR-25793 reached a no-change decision on the same Period-vs-instant question and also pointed flexible scheduling windows to requestedPeriod. A relevant Zulip implementers thread is consistent with that rationale and no conflicting later community evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml keeps Appointment.start and Appointment.end as instant, includes the requested comment on both elements, and places Appointment.requestedPeriod immediately after Appointment.minutesDuration following start/end.

related_jiras.note: Earlier PA no-change issue on whether Appointment should use Period instead of start/end instants; it supports using requestedPeriod for nonspecific scheduling windows.
